stories.headline: Blackstone and Google form $5B TPU cloud joint venture adding 500MW of AI capacity

key_facts.fact: Blackstone and Google are forming a joint venture to create a new TPU cloud company, with Blackstone investing $5 billion to kickstart the business.
key_facts.excerpt: Alternative asset manager Blackstone plans to kickstart the new business with a $5 billion investment that will add 500 MW of capacity in 2027.

key_facts.fact: The new venture will add 500 MW of capacity in 2027, with Google Cloud providing data center capacity, networking and access to its Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).
key_facts.excerpt: Google Cloud said it will provide data center capacity and operations, networking, and access to the Google Cloud Tensor Processing Units (TPUs).

key_facts.fact: The company will be led by CEO Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a longtime Google infrastructure executive, and lets Google expand TPU adoption beyond its own cloud while reducing reliance on Nvidia-centric ecosystems.
key_facts.excerpt: The new company will be led by CEO Benjamin Treynor Sloss... this gives Google a way to expand TPU adoption beyond its own cloud footprint while reducing dependence on NVIDIA-centric ecosystems.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said the venture helps meet growing demand for TPUs, which are optimized for efficiency and performance in the AI era.
key_facts.excerpt: "This joint venture with Blackstone helps meet growing demand for TPUs, which are optimized specifically for efficiency and performance in the AI era," says Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud.

sources.title: Blackstone and Google launch $5B TPU cloud venture with 500MW of AI capacity

stories.headline: AMD's Lisa Su names HBM memory as the new AI chip bottleneck at Computex, backs $10B Taiwan bet

key_facts.fact: At Computex 2026, AMD CEO Lisa Su said high-bandwidth memory (HBM) has replaced advanced packaging as the binding constraint limiting how fast the industry can scale AI chips, affecting AMD, Nvidia and every team booking GPU capacity for 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The warning: high-bandwidth memory has replaced advanced packaging as the constraint that limits how fast anyone in the industry can scale AI chips. That second part applies equally to AMD, NVIDIA, and every team currently booking GPU capacity for 2026.

key_facts.fact: Producing one gigabyte of HBM3E or HBM4 consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity of equivalent DDR5; the three HBM makers (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) have committed their entire 2026 output, and HBM now makes up 63% of AI accelerator component costs, up from 52% in early 2024.
key_facts.excerpt: Producing one gigabyte of HBM3E or HBM4 consumes roughly three times the wafer capacity required to produce the equivalent in DDR5... Epoch AI's chip cost tracker shows HBM now makes up 63% of AI accelerator component costs, up from 52% in early 2024.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the Computex push, Su committed more than $10 billion across Taiwan's electronics ecosystem, targeting advanced packaging capacity at TSMC and an HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung, while also expanding EPYC Venice production to TSMC Arizona.
key_facts.excerpt: Su committed more than $10 billion in investment across Taiwan's electronics ecosystem—targeting advanced packaging capacity at TSMC and an HBM4 supply agreement with Samsung. AMD is also expanding Venice production to TSMC Arizona.

key_facts.fact: AMD's EPYC Venice, the first HPC CPU in volume production on TSMC's 2nm process, brings 256 cores and 512 threads under a Zen 6 architecture, with AMD claiming 70%+ performance and efficiency gains over the current EPYC Turin.
key_facts.excerpt: EPYC Venice is now in volume production on TSMC's 2nm process—making it the first HPC CPU in the industry to reach this node. Venice brings 256 cores and 512 threads under a Zen 6 architecture, with AMD claiming 70%+ performance and efficiency gains over the current EPYC Turin.

sources.title: AMD at COMPUTEX 2026: HBM Memory Is Now AI's Hard Limit
HBM Memory Is Now 63% of AI Chip Costs in 2026

stories.headline: China starts commercial operation of offshore wind-powered underwater AI data center near Shanghai

key_facts.fact: China has started commercial operations at an offshore wind-powered underwater AI data center near Shanghai's Lingang Special Area, housing nearly 2,000 servers in pressure-resistant subsea modules about 35 meters below the surface.
key_facts.excerpt: China has started commercial operations at an offshore wind-powered underwater AI data centre near Shanghai's Lingang Special Area. The facility houses nearly 2,000 servers inside pressure-resistant subsea modules located close to offshore wind turbines. The modules sit about 35 metres below the ocean surface.

key_facts.fact: The project cost about 1.6 billion yuan (around $226 million); it began as a 2.3MW demonstration before expanding into a 24MW commercial operation, with more than 95% of its power drawn from renewable energy.
key_facts.excerpt: The project reportedly cost about ¥1.6 billion, or around US$226 million. The facility was built in stages. It began as a 2.3MW demonstration project before expanding into a 24MW commercial operation... more than 95% of its power comes from renewable energy.

key_facts.fact: The facility uses seawater as part of a passive cooling system and reportedly achieved a Power Usage Effectiveness rating below 1.15, versus closer to 1.5 for traditional enterprise data centers; developers say it cuts electricity use by 22.8%, removes freshwater needs, and reduces land requirements by more than 90%.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese media reports said the facility achieved a Power Usage Effectiveness rating below 1.15... which often operate closer to 1.5. Developers said the Lingang facility reduces electricity use by 22.8% and removes the need for freshwater. They also said it cuts land requirements by more than 90%.

key_facts.fact: The project was developed by the Lingang Special Area Administrative Committee, Shanghai Lingang Special Area Investment Holding Group and HiCloud Technology, with operational agreements signed with China Telecom, Shenergy Group and CCCC Third Harbor Engineering.
key_facts.excerpt: The project was developed through a partnership involving the Lingang Special Area Administrative Committee, Shanghai Lingang Special Area Investment Holding Group, and HiCloud Technology... Operational agreements were also signed with China Telecom, Shenergy Group, and CCCC Third Harbor Engineering.

sources.title: China launches offshore wind-powered underwater AI data centre

stories.headline: Google breaks ground on $15B gigawatt-scale AI data center hub in Visakhapatnam, India

key_facts.fact: Google has broken ground on a major AI infrastructure hub in Visakhapatnam, India, beginning a $15 billion investment planned through 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Google has broken ground on a major AI infrastructure hub in Visakhapatnam, India, beginning a $15 billion investment planned through 2030.

key_facts.fact: The project features India's first gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure, consisting of three data center campuses built in partnership with AdaniConneX and Nxtra by Airtel.
key_facts.excerpt: The project features India's first gigawatt-scale AI infrastructure, consisting of three data center campuses built in partnership with AdaniConneX and Nxtra by Airtel.

key_facts.fact: Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian called the development 'an inflection point for the country's AI-native future'; the Vizag hub integrates a fiber-optic network via the America-India Connect initiative and supports India's goal of 500 GW non-fossil-fuel capacity by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: Thomas Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud, stated the development is "an inflection point for the country's AI-native future"... The Vizag hub integrates a massive fiber-optic network via the America-India Connect initiative... supporting the national goal of 500 GW non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.

sources.title: Google Breaks Ground on Landmark $15 Billion AI Industrial Ecosystem in India

stories.headline: China's LimX Dynamics launches Luna humanoid robot for commercial spaces at ~$43,800

key_facts.fact: Chinese embodied-AI startup LimX Dynamics launched the LimX Luna, a full-size interactive humanoid robot, on May 25, with an official guide price of 298,000 yuan ($43,840), targeting commercial interaction.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese embodied AI startup LimX Dynamics has launched the LimX Luna, a full-size interactive humanoid robot, with an official guide price of 298,000 yuan ($43,840), targeting the commercial interaction sector.

key_facts.fact: LimX Luna stands 160 cm tall with 27 degrees of freedom (excluding end-effectors) and combines high-dynamic motion control with multi-modal interaction.
key_facts.excerpt: Standing 160 centimeters tall with 27 degrees of freedom (excluding end-effectors), LimX Luna integrates high-dynamic motion control with multi-modal interaction capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The robot supports video-based choreography learning, zero-code task programming and intelligent fleet management, positioned as a content and traffic carrier for shopping malls, scenic areas and exhibition venues.
key_facts.excerpt: The robot supports video-based choreography learning, zero-code task programming, and intelligent fleet management, positioning it as a content and traffic carrier for shopping malls, scenic areas, and exhibition venues.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Q1 profit drops 57% as global memory price surge hits its smartphone business

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's Q1 2026 net income tumbled 57% to 4.72 billion yuan ($695 million), double the drop seen in the prior quarter and worse than the average analyst projection of a 52% decline.
key_facts.excerpt: Net income in the first three months of 2026 tumbled 57% to 4.72 billion yuan ($695 million), double the drop in the fourth quarter last year and worse than the average analyst projection of 52%.

key_facts.fact: Revenue fell 11% to 99 billion yuan, the first quarterly decline in nearly three years, as sharp increases in memory prices weighed on the smartphone business.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue fell 11% — the first quarterly decline in nearly three years — to 99 billion yuan, roughly in line with analyst expectations.

key_facts.fact: Xiaomi's Q1 smartphone revenue declined 12.5% year-on-year, with global shipments of about 33.8 million units (down 19%) and mainland China shipments down 35% to 8.7 million units, amid rising DRAM and NAND memory costs.
key_facts.excerpt: Xiaomi's first-quarter 2026 smartphone revenue declined 12.5% year-on-year... The company shipped approximately 33.8 million smartphones globally in Q1, a 19% drop from the previous year. In mainland China, shipments fell 35% year-on-year to 8.7 million units.

key_facts.fact: CEO Lei Jun warned at the company's 17 Max launch that memory chip costs could keep climbing for at least another two years, making smartphone price hikes a structural rather than short-term problem.
key_facts.excerpt: Lei Jun warned that costs for memory chips could keep climbing for at least another two years, making price hikes a structural problem rather than a short-term hiccup.

sources.title: Xiaomi Profit Drops More Than Expected in Global Memory Crunch

stories.headline: Singapore's Doozy Robotics announces seed-backed global expansion ahead of Series A

key_facts.fact: Singapore-based humanoid robotics startup Doozy Robotics announced it is expanding across the US, the Gulf region and Asia, backed by seed-stage investors including Cocoon Capital, as it prepares for a planned Series A round.
key_facts.excerpt: Doozy Robotics is expanding across the U.S., the Gulf region and Asia as the Singapore-based humanoid robotics startup prepares for a planned Series A and scales its AI-powered industrial workforce platform... Backed by investors including Cocoon Capital.

key_facts.fact: Doozy is building a vertically integrated ecosystem combining humanoid robots, autonomous mobile robots and autonomous forklifts coordinated through its Eywa-OS orchestration platform, with its Industrial Super Humanoid slated to launch in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is building a vertically integrated ecosystem combining humanoid robots, autonomous mobile robots and autonomous forklifts coordinated through its Eywa-OS orchestration platform, with its Industrial Super Humanoid slated to launch in the third quarter of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The company reported a global pipeline exceeding $200 million, a $144 million memorandum of understanding with a large industrial customer, and a pilot humanoid deployment with a US pharmaceutical company; named customers and engagements include Daimler, Carrier and VitaQuest.
key_facts.excerpt: Doozy reported that it enters the expansion phase with a global pipeline exceeding $200 million, a $144 million memorandum of understanding with a large industrial customer and a pilot humanoid deployment underway with a U.S. pharmaceutical company. The company also said customers and engagements span organizations including Daimler, Carrier and VitaQuest.
